c1-mechanical-ruling.title: Adjudicate: does advance --mechanical satisfy C1 'records nothing'?
c1-mechanical-ruling.imperative: Attack the commander's ruling that advance --mechanical (and reopen --reason 'control') satisfies C1's 'records nothing'. Read checklist_engine.py at the cited lines. Uphold or overturn explicitly. If overturned, the control's premise is wrong - say so.
c1-mechanical-ruling.finding: UPHELD, and on stronger ground than the reasoning offered. (1) The premise is confirmed AT THE WORLD, not just in source: on a fresh temp gated plan, 'advance g1' with NEITHER flag exits 1 with 'REFUSED: advancing a non-exempt gate requires a running understanding'; 'advance g1 --mechanical' exits 0. One of the two is mechanically required, so C1's 'actions a run mechanically requires' covers it. (2) --mechanical records zero agent characters: the why_trail row is {id,gate,why:null,mechanical:true,ts} and _latest_why_record explicitly skips mechanical rows, so it can never become the digest. attest with no --note leaves satisfied_by=='attested', the engine's own literal. (3) DECISIVE empirical proof, from my M1 mutation: rewriting every advance to --why <narrative prose> and adding --note <prose> to every attest changed NOT ONE of the ten mechanical fields (13/13 still green, prose verified present in why_trail and satisfied_by). The mechanical group is provably DISCONNECTED from agent-authored content, so --mechanical vs --why cannot influence the measurement in either direction. The control's premise is sound; NO re-cut needed. NARROWING on reopen --reason: _append_reopen_marker DOES write the reason string into why_trail, so 'control' is literally agent-authored text that is recorded. It survives C1 only because it is (a) required by the verb, (b) a declared fixed constant, (c) provably field-disconnected by (3). Worth stating as a bounded exception rather than as 'nothing agent-authored was recorded'.
